subject: Reserved capacity implementation playbook + regional capacity decisions
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebulacorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@nebulacorp.com>, cloudops@nebulacorp.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool request & implementation plan kickoff

Hi Marissa,

Following our exec conversation last week: NebulaCorp wants to move to a Redwood dedicated GPU pool for our inference workloads starting H2. High-level ask: reserved baseline capacity with short burst elasticity for batch workloads and a regional failover plan. Rough numbers from our infra team (subject to confirmation):
- Production steady: ~350 qps across mixed seq lengths (avg 256 tokens).
- Peak batch jobs (evenings): spikes that could need ~6 concurrent GPUs for 20-40 minutes.
- Desired latency SLOs: p95 generation < 450ms for short chat flows, background batch tolerance up to 2s.

Questions for your implementation team before the kickoff:
1) Recommended baseline and burst sizes (we currently run on 4xA100 in-house).
2) Autoscaling policy suggestions (cooldown, max burst duration, warm pools).
3) Regional placement: primary in us-west (near our service) with us-east failover; we may want eu-west for EU customers later.
4) Networking and firewall IPs needed for VPC peering and egress allow-lists.
5) Expected lead time to provision dedicated pool and a sample migration/rollout plan.

Can we schedule a 60-min technical kickoff next week with implementation, infra and security? Priya (cc'd) will coordinate availability.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
NebulaCorp

Attachments: none in this initial email
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@nebulacorp.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool request & implementation plan kickoff

Hi Sanjay — thanks, this is clear and a great start. I pulled together an initial implementation playbook and a short provisioning questionnaire for your infra team (attached). High-level responses to your numbered questions below, we can walk through in the kickoff: 

1) Baseline and burst sizing
- Based on the numbers you shared (avg 256 tokens, 350 qps), we typically recommend a baseline of 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs for steady inference with optimized batching and KV caching.
- Burst buffer: allow scaling to 8 GPUs for short windows (up to 30 minutes) to cover evening batch spikes.

2) Autoscaling policy
- Target policy: baseline=4, max_burst=8, burst_window_max=30m, scale_up_aggressiveness=fast (5–10s decision), cool_down=300s.
- We also recommend pre-warming a 1-GPU warm pool for cold-start-sensitive routes.

3) Regional placement
- Primary: us-west1 (lowest latency to your services).
- Secondary: us-east1 with automated DNS failover and warm standby (1–2 GPUs) to keep costs manageable.
- EU rollout: plan for eu-west as a phase 2 once user segmentation warrants it.

4) Networking
- We'll provide a short list of Redwood egress IPs and a VPC peering checklist prior to provisioning.

5) Lead time and rollout
- Typical baseline provisioning: 5–7 business days after PO/contract execution.
- Full migration with canary and rollback: 2 weeks (including load testing).

Next steps I propose:
- Kickoff call: Thu 2027-04-22 10:00 PT (60 min) — Monica (CS), Jonas (runtime), and I will join.
- Complete the attached provisioning questionnaire and return by Tue 2027-04-20 so our infra team can finalize the pool sizing.
- We'll issue a preliminary capacity quote and a DocuSign for the reserved capacity commitment after the kickoff.

Attachments:
- res-cap-playbook-v1.pdf (implementation playbook, runbook checklist)
- nebula_provisioning_questions.xlsx (short questionnaire)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Marissa/Monica — internal notes and quick runbook items before the kickoff. Forwarded comments inline.

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 11:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sanjay — thanks, this is clear and a great start. I pulled together an initial implementation playbook and a short provisioning questionnaire for your infra team (attached). High-level responses to your numbered questions below, we can walk through in the kickoff:

> 1) Baseline and burst sizing

Internal action items (Jonas):
- Validate H100-equivalent sizing vs A100 for Nebula model family — check perf tests (I will run a 1-day perf sweep on our staging pool).
- Provide suggested batching config and target token window (looking at 256 avg, but need distribution).

Monica (CS):
- Confirm Nebula's retention/compliance requirements (logs, KV cache persistence) to decide if warm standby in us-east needs longer cache replication.
- Prep a short customer-facing migration checklist we can share on kickoff.

Aditya (sale/ops):
- Confirm procurement contact and timeline; if they want a 30-day PO we should alert finance for reserved billing.
- Prepare an initial price estimate with 12-month and 36-month reserved options (include burst credits pricing).

Runtime notes (Jonas):
- Autoscale recommendation: fast scale-up with token-weighted batching; implement a burst window limit of 30m and a cooldown of 5m. Also set an emergency fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant if GPU capacity is constrained.

I'll post perf numbers by EOD Mon 4/19 and a draft batching/config suggestion in the shared Drive folder.

— Jonas
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Sanjay — following our internal prep and Jonas' perf planning, here's a consolidated plan and concrete asks so the kickoff is productive.

Confirmed proposal (summary):
- Baseline capacity: 4 x H100-class GPUs (region: us-west1).
- Burst policy: up to 8 GPUs for a maximum continuous burst window of 30 minutes; burst cooldown 300s (5 minutes).
- Warm standby in us-east1 with 1–2 GPUs for automated failover; cache warmup via background replication to reduce cold-starts.
- Autoscale behavior: aggressive scale-up (decisions within 5–10s), smoother scale-down with 5-minute cooldown.
- Fallback model variant: configure an automatic fallback to a quantized 8-bit variant if cluster capacity drops below baseline during region-wide events.

Kickoff meeting: Thu 2027-04-22 10:00 PT (60 minutes) — invite attached calendar; proposed agenda below. Please confirm or propose an alternative slot.

Agenda (60m):
- 10m: Introductions & scope alignment (Marissa / Sanjay)
- 15m: Capacity sizing & perf assumptions (Jonas)
- 15m: Autoscaling/operational runbook (Monica)
- 10m: Networking / security checklist (Aditya)
- 10m: Next steps, PO/contract timeline, deliverables (Marissa)

Pre-kickoff asks (please complete by Tue 2027-04-20):
- Return nebula_provisioning_questions.xlsx with environment details (VPC CIDRs, expected qps by route, retention compliance).
- Provide procurement contact and an expected PO lead time.
- Confirm whether EU region should be included in phase 1 or deferred to phase 2.

Procurement note: we will prepare a reserved capacity quote with a DocuSign package (link below) after the kickoff. If you need a preliminary estimate before the call, let me know and Aditya will share a draft.
